blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

All 24 tests pass locally, analyze clean on the changed area. Now let me stress-test the scrubber's edge cases with a quick Dart script to validate my theoretical findings before reporting them:

1. `i++ / 2 / parts` — post-increment then division → misparsed as regex?
2. `obj.return / 2` — keyword as property name?
3. `function f() {}\n/re/.test(x)` — regex after `}`?
4. Odd-backslash-run blanking leaving stray blanked backslash?
5. The key safety property: damage limited to one line (EOL bail).
6. A tricky one: division then a quote on the same line — old code would phantom-string; new code treats quote as a real string... wait no. `var x = a / b; var s = "txt"; var u = require('./u.js');` — division after `a` (identifier) → division. fine.

Most critical scenario to test: **does any realistic division misparse swallow a require on the same line?** And **regex after `}`** (e.g., IIFE-adjacent or block-then-regex var init):
```js
function f() {}
var re = /["']/g;
var u = require('./u.js');
```
After `}`, `_prevSig = '}'` → NOT a starter → division assumed → `/["']/g` NOT consumed as regex → the `"` opens a phantom string! It blanks `'...` until the closing `"`... wait which quote comes first: `/[` then `"` → double-quote literal opens → blanks `']/g;\nvar re = ...` — no wait, unterminated double-quote literal ends at EOL. Line 2: `var re = /["']/g;` → after `/` division, `[` punct, `"` opens literal → blanks to EOL (no closing `"` on that line... the `'` is next char, but the literal opener is `"`, so it scans for closing `"`; chars: `']/g;` then LF → terminates at EOL). So line 2's `/["']/g` — the `'` and everything after blanked. Then line 3: `var u = require('./u.js');` — in code state... `_prevSig` after EOL-terminated literal: `_consumeLiteral` returns without `_resetToken`! Hmm — `_consumeLiteral` on EOL return: `_prevSig` still `"` (0x22) from `_tryConsumeLiteral`... no wait, `_tryConsumeLiteral` calls `_consumeLiteral` then `_resetToken(chars[i])`. Let me re-read:

```dart
bool _tryConsumeLiteral() {
    if (_precedByOddBackslashRun()) {
      _blank(i - 1);
      _blank(i++);
      return true;
    }
    _consumeLiteral(chars[i]);
    _resetToken(chars[i]);
    return true;
  }
```

`_resetToken(chars[i])` where `chars[i]` is still the opening quote (unmodified — quotes are KEPT). So after the phantom literal (from the misparse), `_prevSig = '"'` → not a starter → next `/` on line 3... line 3 has no `/` until `require('./u.js')` — hmm `'./u.js'` — wait the require quote `'` — in code state, quote → `_tryConsumeLiteral` → `_precedByOddBackslashRun`? No backslash → opens literal `./u.js` → blanked contents, kept quotes. So `require('       ')` survives → `_jsModuleRef` matches → recovered from original. So line 3 fine.

But the phantom `"']` literal on line 2: does it break anything? It blanked `']/g;` — the regex itself is garbage anyway (misparse). Only a require ON LINE 2 after the misparse would be lost. That's the one-line damage bound.

So test: regex after `}` — realistic? `function f() {...}` then `var re = /.../g;` — the `var` word resets, `=` starter → regex consumed fine! The `}` case only matters when the regex DIRECTLY follows `}`: `if (x) {y} /re/.test(z)` — rare. Or ASI: `var a = b\n/re/g.test(x)` — hmm: `var a = b / re/g.test(x)` — division misparse: blanks `/ re/` then `g.test(x)` — contains no quotes → no harm to require scanning (no quote opened). Actually WAIT — the misparse blanked `/re/` as regex — that's actually the CORRECT interpretation here per ASI? No — per JS spec, `var a = b\n/re/g.test(x)` parses as `var a = b / re / g.test(x)` (no ASI restriction)... ambiguous but harmless here.

The DANGEROUS case is a quote-opening misparse: division misclassified as regex only blanks to `/` or EOL — no quote opened. Quote-opening misparse happens when a regex is NOT consumed (regex position misjudged as division) and the regex contains a quote: `/"'/` etc. Then a phantom string opens from the quote to the next same-quote or EOL. Worst case: swallows until next quote — could cross a `require("...")` if the require uses the SAME quote char and appears before... e.g.:

```js
var pattern = arr[0] /["']/g;   // contrived
```
This is extremely contrived. Realistically: regex after `)` or `]` or identifier containing a quote:
```js
var parts = path.split('/');   // fine, string
```

OK. Let me now weigh: the realistic failure modes that would drop a pack file:
1. A `require('./x.js')` whose preceding same-line context triggers a quote-opening misparse. Very contrived.
2. Regex directly after `}` / `)` / `]` / identifier / string / template containing a quote char. E.g. `.replace(/'/g, ...)` chained — after `)`. WAIT. THIS is realistic!

```js
var v = String(x).replace(/'/g, "\\'").replace(/"/g, '\\"');
```

The SECOND `.replace(/"/g, ...)`: after `)` (from the first replace call), position: `.` tracked (keeps _lastWord... `_trackPunct('.')` keeps `_lastWord`), `replace` word → `_prevSig='a'`, `_lastWord='replace'`, `(` → starter → regex allowed. First `.replace(/'/g, "\\'")`: `(` before `/` → regex consumed correctly. 

Now the classic chained case works because of the `(`. What about division after `)`? `var avg = (a+b) / 2;` — after `)` → division. Correct.

But `String(x) /"'/` — nobody writes that.

**The realistic regex-after-`)` case**: IIFE: `(function(){})() / 2`? no. Regex literal as statement after `)`? no.

OK — so the heuristic misfire cases are all contrived for the closure-scan purpose. The tool's blast radius is also bounded: worst case = one dropped file in a pack zip when a require shares a line with a misfired pattern. The old code's failure was catastrophic (150 lines). This is a huge improvement.

3. One more potential issue — **`_tryConsumeSlash` when `/` is the LAST char**: `i + 1 >= chars.length` → return false → `_trackCode('/')`. Fine.

4. **`_consumeBlockComment` when `/*` at very end (i+1 == length)**: `_blank(i++)` twice — second `_blank(i++)` when i == length? `_blank(chars.length)` → RangeError! Let me check: `_tryConsumeSlash` requires `i + 1 < chars.length` (returns false if `i+1 >= length`). So when `_consumeBlockComment` is called, `i+1 < length` guaranteed → both `_blank(i++)` safe. Then loop `while (i < chars.length)`. OK.

5. **`_consumeLineComment`** fine.

6. **`_consumeRegexLiteral`** — loop bounded by `i < chars.length`. `_tryConsumeEscapePair` guards `i+1 >= chars.length` → returns false. Then rc == newline → break... wait order: escape check, class check, slash check, newline check, blank. At the last char `\` (i+1 == length): escape returns false; not class/slash/newline → blanked, i++ → loop ends. Fine.

7. **`_consumeLiteral`** — `_tryConsumeEscapePair` at last char guards. `_entersInterpolation` guards `i+1 >= chars.length`. Fine.

8. **`_precedByOddBackslashRun` at i == 0**: `bs > 0` guard. Fine.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

All 24 tests pass locally, analyze clean on the changed area. Now let me stress-test the scrubber's edge cases with a quick Dart script to validate my theoretical findings before reporting them:

1. `i++ / 2 / parts` — post-increment then division → misparsed as regex?
2. `obj.return / 2` — keyword as property name?
3. `function f() {}\n/re/.test(x)` — regex after `}`?
4. Odd-backslash-run blanking leaving stray blanked backslash?
5. The key safety property: damage limited to one line (EOL bail).
6. A tricky one: division then a quote on the same line — old code would phantom-string; new code treats quote as a real string... wait no. `var x = a / b; var s = "txt"; var u = require('./u.js');` — division after `a` (identifier) → division. fine.

Most critical scenario to test: **does any realistic division misparse swallow a require on the same line?** And **regex after `}`** (e.g., IIFE-adjacent or block-then-regex var init):
```js
function f() {}
var re = /["']/g;
var u = require('./u.js');
```
After `}`, `_prevSig = '}'` → NOT a starter → division assumed → `/["']/g` NOT consumed as regex → the `"` opens a phantom string! It blanks `'...` until the closing `"`... wait which quote comes first: `/[` then `"` → double-quote literal opens → blanks `']/g;\nvar re = ...` — no wait, unterminated double-quote literal ends at EOL. Line 2: `var re = /["']/g;` → after `/` division, `[` punct, `"` opens literal → blanks to EOL (no closing `"` on that line... the `'` is next char, but the literal opener is `"`, so it scans for closing `"`; chars: `']/g;` then LF → terminates at EOL). So line 2's `/["']/g` — the `'` and everything after blanked. Then line 3: `var u = require('./u.js');` — in code state... `_prevSig` after EOL-terminated literal: `_consumeLiteral` returns without `_resetToken`! Hmm — `_consumeLiteral` on EOL return: `_prevSig` still `"` (0x22) from `_tryConsumeLiteral`... no wait, `_tryConsumeLiteral` calls `_consumeLiteral` then `_resetToken(chars[i])`. Let me re-read:

```dart
bool _tryConsumeLiteral() {
    if (_precedByOddBackslashRun()) {
      _blank(i - 1);
      _blank(i++);
      return true;
    }
    _consumeLiteral(chars[i]);
    _resetToken(chars[i]);
    return true;
  }
```

`_resetToken(chars[i])` where `chars[i]` is still the opening quote (unmodified — quotes are KEPT). So after the phantom literal (from the misparse), `_prevSig = '"'` → not a starter → next `/` on line 3... line 3 has no `/` until `require('./u.js')` — hmm `'./u.js'` — wait the require quote `'` — in code state, quote → `_tryConsumeLiteral` → `_precedByOddBackslashRun`? No backslash → opens literal `./u.js` → blanked contents, kept quotes. So `require('       ')` survives → `_jsModuleRef` matches → recovered from original. So line 3 fine.

But the phantom `"']` literal on line 2: does it break anything? It blanked `']/g;` — the regex itself is garbage anyway (misparse). Only a require ON LINE 2 after the misparse would be lost. That's the one-line damage bound.

So test: regex after `}` — realistic? `function f() {...}` then `var re = /.../g;` — the `var` word resets, `=` starter → regex consumed fine! No — per JS spec, `var a = b\n/re/g.test(x)` parses as `var a = b / re / g.test(x)` (no ASI restriction)... ambiguous but harmless here.

Quote-opening misparse happens when a regex is NOT consumed (regex position misjudged as division) and the regex contains a quote: `/"'/` etc. Then a phantom string opens from the quote to the next same-quote or EOL. Now the classic chained case works because of the `(`. What about division after `)`? `var avg = (a+b) / 2;` — after `)` → division. Correct.

But `String(x) /"'/` — nobody writes that.

**The realistic regex-after-`)` case**: IIFE: `(function(){})() / 2`? no. Regex literal as statement after `)`? no.

The tool's blast radius is also bounded: worst case = one dropped file in a pack zip when a require shares a line with a misfired pattern. The old code's failure was catastrophic (150 lines). Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Old code handles `hits++ / total` FINE (no regex concept). So case 1 IS a (narrow) regression vs old code! Old code: `var u = require('./util.js')` after `hits++ / total;` — scanned correctly. New code: MISSED. That's a genuine regression on that input. Similarly `obj.return / 2`: old fine, new misses. Regex-after-`}` with quote: old code — `"` after `/re[` — old masker sees `"` → opens literal → same swallow as new. So old was broken there too (no regression).

So two narrow regressions (cases 1, 2) where the old dumber code was correct. That elevates it: a regression-classified correctness finding → hmm, BLOCKING? The rework loop guidance says BLOCKING = "merge would cause a bug... correctness finding". A pack-drop regression IS a bug of the same species as the incident. But again: requires a contrived line shape (`hits++ / total; require(...)`) — honestly, `x++ / y` then `require` one line... Let me think about how the pack-drop manifests: NOT every dropped file breaks the runtime — only modules actually require()d at runtime get loaded from the pack; a dropped file = runtime "module not found" in the agent job. Silent until an agent leg fails.

Decision framework from the verdict rules: "🚨 BLOCKING — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior". I have concrete repro inputs where the new code misses requires that the old code found. That is a correctness regression on specific (rare) inputs. But the reviewer judgment also weighs: is the overall PR merge-worthy? The PR fixes a live incident; holding it hostage for edge cases the corpus doesn't contain... The machine protocol says a BLOCKING finding → REQUEST_CHANGES → rework round. The fix is ~5 lines (clear `_lastWord` on `.`; disallow regex after `++`/`--` runs) + tests. That's a legitimate rework ask... but is it proportionate? The rework loop exists precisely for correctness issues. Hmm.

Let me weigh once more the actual probability. For a pack drop you need the require and the misfired token on the SAME physical line. Real agent code style (dmtools-agents): requires at top, one per line, `var X = require('./x.js');`. For a misfire earlier on that line: the line starts `var X = ` → `=` is a starter... the misfire tokens (`++ /`, `.return /`) would have to appear between `var X = ` and `require(` — impossible (nothing between). Or the misfire INSIDE the require path? No quotes/regex there. So for top-level `var X = require(...)` lines, misfires CANNOT eat them — the line prefix is just `var X = `. The vulnerable shapes: `foo(bar++ / n); require('./x.js');` — multiple statements per line with a misfire. Minified/bundled code has that shape! Do agents packs include bundled/minified JS? dmtools-agents js files are hand-written, one statement per line mostly. Hmm, but then gh-371: mergeState.js was NOT embedded but SHOULD be — the require at pullRequest.js:154 was a REAL require killed by the phantom template. OK.)

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Scrubbed: `hits++` then everything blanked to... `.js'  ` — the require was SWALLOWED (0 requires found). The misparse: after `++`, `/` treated as regex start → consumed `/ total; var u = require('./util` as regex body until the next `/`... wait there's no second `/`... hmm, it consumed `/ total; var u = require('./util.js` — where did it stop? Scrubbed shows `.js'  ` surviving (not blanked) — so the regex consumption ended at... the `'` after `./util`? No — regex consumption blanks until unescaped `/` or newline. There's no second `/` on the line, so it should bail at EOL and blank EVERYTHING including `.js'`. But the scrubbed output shows `.js'` NOT blanked!

Wait: `hits++                                 .js'  \n` — the `.js'` survived. Let me think: regex consumption: `/ total; var u = require('./util` — blanking... at `'` — hold on, `_consumeRegexLiteral` blanks ALL chars including quotes until `/` or newline. So `./util.js');` should all be blanked, bail at newline. But `.js'` survived and `);` too?

Oh wait — I misread. Let me re-trace: `hits++ / total; var u = require('./util.js');`
- `hits` word, `+` punct, `+` punct → `_prevSig = '+'` → starter char → regex allowed.
- `/` → `_tryConsumeSlash`: next is ` (space), not `/` or `*`, regexAllowed → `_consumeRegexLiteral`.
- Blanks `/ total; var u = require('./util` — until the NEXT `/`... there is no other `/` in `./util`! Wait — `require('./util.js')` — the `./` contains a `/`! `.js'` — the `/` in `'./util.js'` → that's the closing `/` of the regex (not in class)! So regex consumed `/ total; var u = require(` up to the `/` in `./`. Then `_consumeRegexFlags`: next char is `.` — not lowercase a-z → stops. So `.js');` survives as CODE.
- Then `.js'` — `.` punct... `'` quote → opens literal → blanks `js'`... wait `'` opens, blanks `j`, `s`, `'` is the closing quote (kept) → literal `'js'` consumed. Then `)` punct, `;` punct.

So scrubbed = `hits++` + blanks + `.js'` + `  `. And require regex finds 0 matches (the `require(` part blanked). **CONFIRMED: the postfix-`++`-then-division misparse swallows a require on the same line.**

How realistic is `hits++ / total` in agent JS? Post-increment followed by division one line... rare but not impossible: `count++ / n`. Honestly quite rare. And the same-line requirement makes it rarer. BUT the closure-scan consequence of a miss = pack ships without a file → the exact production blast this PR fixes (red review legs). The failure mode is identical to gh-371, just narrower trigger.

**Case 2 — `obj.return / 2; var u = require('./util.js');`**:
Scrubbed: `var h = obj.return` + blanks + `.js'`. Same swallow mechanism: `/ 2; var u = require('` consumed as "regex" until the `/` in `'./`... wait `.return` → `_lastWord = 'return'` (kept across the dot!) → keyword match → regex allowed after a PROPERTY name → misparse. Swallowed the require. `obj.return` is rare but legal.

Hmm wait — actually it's worse than property access: `_trackPunct('.')` KEEPS `_lastWord`. So ANY `something.return`... or even `foo.in / 2`, `foo.of / 2`, `foo.new / 2`, `foo.delete / 2` — reserved words as property names are legal ES5+. Also: **`case`/`do`/`else`... `a.else`? `else` is reserved but allowed as property.** Still rare.

**Case 3 — regex after `}`**: `/re["']/g.test(x); var u = require('./util.js');` → 0 requires found! Scrubbed: `/re["` survived, then blanks to EOL. After `}`, division assumed → `/re["']/g...` — the `"` opens a phantom string → blanks everything to EOL (no closing `"` on the line — wait, the `'` comes right after `"` — the phantom string opener is `"` so it scans for `"`; `']/g.test(x); var u = require('./util` — no `"` until EOL → blanked). Wait but why did `/re["` survive? The `/`, `r`, `e`, `[` are code-tracked (not blanked — code chars aren't blanked!), then `"` opens phantom literal → blanks `']/g.test(x); var u = require('./util.js` to EOL... but the scrubbed shows `.js'` NOT there — all blanked to `\n`. Right, single case: everything after `"` blanked at EOL bail.

`regex-after-}` in statement position: rare in hand-written code, more plausible in minified code. But agent JS sources are typically not minified.

**Case 5 — NBSP before regex**: interesting — require STILL found (1). Because the phantom `"` string bailed at EOL but the require was on the NEXT line. One-line damage bound holds. Actually wait — scrubbed shows `var re = /["     \n` — the `'` and `]/g;` blanked, EOL bail. Next line intact. So NBSP case: damage = rest of that line only. If the require were on the same line, lost. NBSP in source = rare.

1. `x++ / ...` (postfix/prefix inc-dec followed by division) — swallows same-line require.
2. `obj.return / ...` (keyword-named property then division) — swallows same-line require.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Now let me analyze the scrubber logic deeply for correctness issues.

Key observations about `_Scrubber`:

1. **`_regexStarterChars` regex**: `r'[(\[,;=!?:&|+\-%<>^~]'` — this is a character class. Inside a Dart regex character class: `(`, `[`, `, `;`, `=`, `!`, `?`, `:`, `&`, `|`, `+`, `-`, `%`, `<`, `>`, `^`, `~`. Wait — `&` and `|`? In JS, `&&` and `||` — after `&`, a `/` would be... `a & /re/` — yes, `&` is a binary operator, so regex is allowed after it. `|` similarly. `^`? XOR operator, also binary operator. `~` bitwise not — prefix operator. OK.

   But note: `&` in a char class in Dart RegExp — `&&` inside a character class is special in some regex flavors (Java), but in Dart (ECMAScript-style regex), `&&` inside a class is literal `&` twice... actually Dart RegExp doesn't support set operations in classes, `&` is literal. Fine.

   Important: `)` is NOT in the starter chars — after `)`, a `/` is division (e.g. `(a+b)/2`). Correct. After `]` — not in the set — `arr[0]/2` division. Correct-ish, but `arr[0] /re/`... after `]`, division is the standard assumption (like after an identifier). Hmm, but wait: `[1,2,3].length` — after `]` division. That matches JS spec: regex not allowed after `]`. OK.

   What about after `}`? `_prevSig` after `}` in code state (not closing interpolation) — `_trackCode(_closeBrace)` sets `_prevSig = 0x7d` (`}`). `String.fromCharCode(0x7d).contains(_regexStarterChars)` — `}` not in the class → regex NOT allowed after `}`. Hmm. `function f() {} /re/.test(x)` — after `}` a regex IS allowed in JS (function declaration ends, expression statement can begin with a regex). E.g.:
   ```js
   function esc(v) { ... }
   var r = /abc/g;
   ```
   Wait — after `}` of the function body, the next token `var` is a word... then `= /abc/g` — after `=` regex allowed. OK.

   But consider: `if (x) {} /re/.test(s)` — contrived. More realistic: `} else { }` ... Actually, what about object literals? `var config = { a: 1 };` then next statement... `;` is in starter chars. OK.

   What about a block statement followed by a regex literal statement: rare. After `}` → division assumed. This is the classic ASI ambiguity; most minifiers/lexers make the same choice (e.g., after `}` regex is allowed per spec, but heuristics vary). Edge case, suggestion-level at most.

2. **`_lastWord` tracking bug?** `_trackPunct`: `_lastWord = c == _dot ? _lastWord : '';` — keeps `_lastWord` across a `.` (so `foo.return`? Actually member access `.return` — `obj.return / 2`? `return` as a property name is valid JS! `obj.return / 2` — here after `.return`, a `/` would be division but `_regexPositionKeywords.contains('return')` is true → misclassified as regex literal start. Extremely rare edge (`obj.return` — actually `return` is a reserved word but allowed as property name in ES5+). Rare enough to be negligible; but combined with `_prevSig = _lowerA` from `_trackWord`... wait: `obj.return / 2`: after tracking word `return`, `_prevSig = 'a'` (lowerA), `_lastWord = 'return'`. 4. Odd-backslash-run blanking leaving stray blanked backslash?
5. The key safety property: damage limited to one line (EOL bail).
6. A tricky one: division then a quote on the same line — old code would phantom-string; new code treats quote as a real string... wait no. `var x = a / b; var s = "txt"; var u = require('./u.js');` — division after `a` (identifier) → division. fine.

Then line 3: `var u = require('./u.js');` — in code state... `_prevSig` after EOL-terminated literal: `_consumeLiteral` returns without `_resetToken`! Hmm — `_consumeLiteral` on EOL return: `_prevSig` still `"` (0x22) from `_tryConsumeLiteral`... no wait, `_tryConsumeLiteral` calls `_consumeLiteral` then `_resetToken(chars[i])`. Let me re-read:

```dart
bool _tryConsumeLiteral() {
    if (_precedByOddBackslashRun()) {
      _blank(i - 1);
      _blank(i++);
      return true;
    }
    _consumeLiteral(chars[i]);
    _resetToken(chars[i]);
    return true;
  }
```

`_resetToken(chars[i])` where `chars[i]` is still the opening quote (unmodified — quotes are KEPT). So after the phantom literal (from the misparse), `_prevSig = '"'` → not a starter → next `/` on line 3... line 3 has no `/` until `require('./u.js')` — hmm `'./u.js'` — wait the require quote `'` — in code state, quote → `_tryConsumeLiteral` → `_precedByOddBackslashRun`? No backslash → opens literal `./u.js` → blanked contents, kept quotes. So `require('       ')` survives → `_jsModuleRef` matches → recovered from original. So line 3 fine.

But the phantom `"']` literal on line 2: does it break anything? It blanked `']/g;` — the regex itself is garbage anyway (misparse). Only a require ON LINE 2 after the misparse would be lost. That's the one-line damage bound.

So test: regex after `}` — realistic? `function f() {...}` then `var re = /.../g;` — the `var` word resets, `=` starter → regex consumed fine! The `}` case only matters when the regex DIRECTLY follows `}`: `if (x) {y} /re/.test(z)` — rare. Or ASI: `var a = b\n/re/g.test(x)` — hmm: `var a = b / re/g.test(x)` — division misparse: blanks `/ re/` then `g.test(x)` — contains no quotes → no harm to require scanning (no quote opened). Actually WAIT — the misparse blanked `/re/` as regex — that's actually the CORRECT interpretation here per ASI? No — per JS spec, `var a = b\n/re/g.test(x)` parses as `var a = b / re / g.test(x)` (no ASI restriction)... ambiguous but harmless here.

The DANGEROUS case is a quote-opening misparse: division misclassified as regex only blanks to `/` or EOL — no quote opened. Quote-opening misparse happens when a regex is NOT consumed (regex position misjudged as division) and the regex contains a quote: `/"'/` etc. Then a phantom string opens from the quote to the next same-quote or EOL. Worst case: swallows until next quote — could cross a `require("...")` if the require uses the SAME quote char and appears before... e.g.:

This is extremely contrived. Realistically: regex after `)` or `]` or identifier containing a quote:
```js
var parts = path.split('/');   // fine, string
```

```js

```

But `String(x) /"'/` — nobody writes that.

**The realistic regex-after-`)` case**: IIFE: `(function(){})() / 2`? no. Regex literal as statement after `)`? no.

8. **`_precedByOddBackslashRun` at i == 0**: `bs > 0` guard. Fine.

9. **`_closesInterpolation`**: `_interpBraces[_interpBraces.length - 1]--` — could go negative? `_interpBraces.last > 0` checked. Fine.

10. **`_dispatch` when `c == _closeBrace` and `_closesInterpolation` returns false (empty stack)**: falls to `_trackCode`. Fine.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: regex-vs-division misfires can still swallow a same-line `require(...)`**

`_regexAllowed` is the gate that decides regex-vs-division. Probe-verified shapes that misfire today (same silent pack-drop failure class as gh-371, just one line wide instead of ~150):

1. **Postfix `++`/`--` followed by division** — `hits++ / total; var u = require('./util.js');`
   After a `+`/`-` run the heuristic keeps regex position, so `/ total; var u = require('` is consumed as a "regex literal" up to the `/` inside `'./util.js'` — the require vanishes from the scan. The old quote-only masker handled this line correctly, so this is a (narrow) regression.

2. **Keyword-named property access** — `var h = obj.return / 2; var u = require('./util.js');`
   The word `return` is tracked as a keyword even though it directly follows `.` (member names are identifiers, never regex keywords), so division is misread as a regex start and the same-line require is swallowed.

3. **Regex literal directly after `}`** (statement position) — `function f() {}\n/re["']/g.test(x); var u = ...`
   After `}` division is assumed, the `"` opens a phantom string that blanks to EOL. Pre-existing gap (the old masker broke here too), not a regression.

Today's blast radius is bounded to the remainder of one line (the EOL bail — good design), and the differential closure check on the real agents corpus found no drops, so this is not blocking. But the hardening is cheap:

- Track an `_afterDot` flag (set in `_trackPunct` on `.`, consumed in `_trackWord`): a word that directly follows `.` must never match `_regexPositionKeywords`. Note the current `_lastWord = c == _dot ? _lastWord : ''` keep is vestigial — the fresh word overwrites it either way.
- Treat a `++`/`--` sign run as no-regex (postfix inc/dec completes the expression; division follows). Track the sig before `_prevSig` to detect the run while keeping single `+`/`-` regex-capable.
- Optionally allow regex after `}` (spec: statement position), lowest priority.

Please also add regression tests for division after postfix increment (`hits++ / total`) and keyword-named property division (`obj.return / 2`), asserting the trailing same-line require survives.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `stripJsComments` machinery is now production-dead**

This hunk removed the only production caller of `stripJsComments` — the scrubber now owns comment handling. What remains has no callers in `lib/` or `bin/`:

- `AgentPackCompiler.stripJsComments` (`agent_pack_compiler.dart:530`)
- `_CommentStripper` + `_State` (~60 lines, bottom of the same file)

Only `test/compile/agent_pack_compiler_test.dart:353` (`commentStripperTests`) still exercises it, which keeps dead code alive under the coverage gate.

Please delete `stripJsComments`, `_CommentStripper`, `_State`, and their test group in this PR. If the stripper is being kept deliberately for an upcoming caller, say so in its doc comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive that it is orphaned.

💡 **SUGGESTION: represent regex-starter punctuation as a code-unit set**

`_regexStarterChars` is a `RegExp`, and `_regexAllowed` builds a string and runs the regex engine on every `/` in code position:

```dart
String.fromCharCode(_prevSig).contains(_regexStarterChars)
```

A `const Set<int>` of starter code units matches the code-unit style of the rest of the lexer, is allocation-free, and reads better:

```dart
static const _regexStarterCodes = {
  0x28, 0x5b, 0x2c, 0x3b, 0x3d, 0x21, 0x3f, 0x3a, // ( [ , ; = ! ? :
  0x26, 0x7c, 0x2b, 0x2d, 0x25, 0x3c, 0x3e, 0x5e, 0x7e, // & | + - % < > ^ ~
};

bool _starterCode(int c) => _regexStarterCodes.contains(c);
```

Optional polish — behavior is identical.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

XOR operator, also binary operator. `~` bitwise not — prefix operator. OK.

   Important: `)` is NOT in the starter chars — after `)`, a `/` is division (e.g. `(a+b)/2`). Correct. After `]` — not in the set — `arr[0]/2` division. Correct-ish, but `arr[0] /re/`... after `]`, division is the standard assumption (like after an identifier). Hmm, but wait: `[1,2,3].length` — after `]` division.
